chunks: 3. My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-Tayyar, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said:

There is no action involving contraction (fear/awe) or expansion (delight/calmness) among that which Allah has commanded or prohibited, except that it contains a trial and decree from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.ابْتِلَاء: Trial; a test or examination from God
key_terms.بَسْط: Expansion; spiritual state of delight, calmness, or ease
key_terms.قَبْض: Contraction; spiritual state of awe, fear, or constraint

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of fear and delight in response to divine commands and prohibitions?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates that every divine command or prohibition inherently triggers a spiritual contraction (qabd) or expansion (bast) within the soul, serving as a continuous divine trial (ibtala') and decree (qada'). This perspective underscores the dynamic nature of faith, where internal spiritual states are not merely psychological reactions but essential mechanisms for testing human piety and obedience to God's will.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 3. My father (RA) said: Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah said, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Fudalah ibn Ayyub, on the authority of Hamzah ibn Muhammad la-Tayyar that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said: “
There is no action which Allah has commanded to do or which Allah has prohibited from doing, and which causes fear or delight, which is not a trial decreed from Allah, the mighty and High.”
